answer: A practical defense is a proof-of-personhood gate for high-value actions: an agent must obtain a scarce, nontransferable credential from an in-person check or trusted local attestation, then stake it to join markets. Rate limits and slashing bind each credential to one active identity, so minting a hundred accounts does not multiply influence. The attacker must recruit real people, pass checks, and lock capital at risk—costs that rise with every extra identity. A dune, lagoon, or haven can host a verifier, but scenery alone proves nothing.
